subject.title: fix(http): harden network and response boundaries

question: Should an aborted but still-running OS DNS lookup continue counting against the pool’s concurrency limit, or may the limit apply only to active callers?
rationale: The patch intentionally improves caller progress by releasing capacity immediately, but that changes the limit from bounding real DNS operations to bounding only non-aborted callers; tests cannot choose that resource and security policy.

options.title: Preserve the physical lookup bound
options.body: Track unresolved lookup operations separately and do not start more underlying lookups than the configured limit, while discarding results for aborted callers.

options.title: Accept caller-slot semantics
options.body: Keep immediate slot recycling and explicitly document that aborted uncancellable lookups may temporarily exceed the configured underlying-operation limit.

options.title: Split the pool change
options.body: Land the independent HTTP and NAT64 corrections while holding the cancellation-capacity change for a narrower design review.

recommendation.title: Preserve the physical lookup bound
recommendation.body: Track unresolved lookup operations separately and do not start more underlying lookups than the configured limit, while discarding results for aborted callers.

likelyOwner.reason: This contributor has the strongest recent history signal across provider-server runtime and reliability behavior adjacent to the decision.
